name: William Walworth
description: Lord Mayor of London during the revolt; a wealthy fishmonger by trade. Present alongside Richard II at the 15 June 1381 meeting with Wat Tyler at Smithfield. Chroniclers' accounts of the exact trigger vary in detail but agree that when an altercation broke out between Tyler and members of the royal party, Walworth struck the first blow against Tyler; squire Ralph Standish then stabbed him fatally. Walworth immediately moved to raise the City militia, helping disperse the remaining rebel crowd after Richard rode forward to address them, and was knighted by the King on the spot for his role in ending the confrontation.
narrative_function: The man who kills Wat Tyler and, in the same afternoon, helps re-establish royal and civic authority over London.
